_meta.indication: SOFDRA is indicated for the treatment of primary axillary hyperhidrosis in adults and pediatric patients 9 years of age and older.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled pivotal efficacy and safety study; SB gel 15% vs vehicle gel, applied topically once daily for 42 days.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults and pediatric patients ≥9 years of age with primary axillary hyperhidrosis.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: proportion of subjects with ≥2 point improvement in HDSM-Ax-7 scale score from baseline to end of treatment, and change from baseline to EOT in gravimetric sweat production (GSP).
pivotal_trials.n: 350 subjects randomized (SB gel 15% N=173, Vehicle N=177).
pivotal_trials.result: ≥2 point HDSM-Ax-7 improvement: 50.4% SB vs 32.1% vehicle; treatment difference 18.3 (95% CI 8.0, 28.7); p=0.0005. Change in GSP p=0.0019; median change -127.8 mg SB vs -100.3 mg vehicle.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled pivotal efficacy and safety study; SB gel 15% vs vehicle gel, applied topically once daily for 42 days.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults and pediatric patients ≥9 years of age with primary axillary hyperhidrosis.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: proportion of subjects with ≥2 point improvement in HDSM-Ax-7 scale score from baseline to end of treatment, and change from baseline to EOT in gravimetric sweat production (GSP).
pivotal_trials.n: 351 subjects randomized (SB gel 15% N=180, Vehicle N=171).
pivotal_trials.result: ≥2 point HDSM-Ax-7 improvement: 63.3% SB vs 47.1% vehicle; treatment difference 16.2 (95% CI 5.4, 26.9); p=0.0040. Change in GSP p=0.0296; median change -142.6 mg SB vs -134.2 mg vehicle.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥2%) are dry mouth, blurred vision, application site pain/erythema, mydriasis, and urinary retention. In pooled controlled trials (SOFDRA N=353 vs Vehicle N=347): dry mouth 14% vs 0.6%, vision blurred 9% vs 0.3%, mydriasis 7% vs 0, urinary retention 2% vs 0.
target_moa: Sofpironium bromide is a small-molecule quaternary ammonium anticholinergic (analogue of glycopyrrolate) that reduces sweat production as a selective, competitive inhibitor of muscarinic receptor type 3 (M3), the predominant receptor in axillary eccrine sweat glands.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because there were no issues that warranted an advisory committee discussion.

basis.text: The application was reviewed under Standard (not Priority) review.

summary.text: SOFDRA was approved as a 505(b)(1) new molecular entity under standard review, without accelerated approval or special expedited designations. NDA 217347 first received a Complete Response on September 22, 2023, and was approved after the sponsor's complete-response amendment.

citations.quote: The applicant submitted a 505(b)(1) application for their proposed product, sofipironium bromide topical gel, 15% (12.45% free base) to treat primary axillary hyperhidrosis in adults and children aged 9 years and older.

Priority or Standard	Standard
Submit Date(s)	September 23, 2022
After review, on September 22, 2023, the Agency issued a Complete Response (CR) for NDA 217347 for the following reasons:
We acknowledge receipt of your amendment dated December 20, 2023, which constituted a complete response to our September 22, 2023, action letter.
